newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU traders see possible cut in flour export refund.
newsitem.headline: EU traders see possible cut in flour export refund.

text.p: European grain industry sources said they were waiting on Tuesday to see whether the European Commission would reduce its standing refund for wheat flour exports in the wake of Monday's abolition of a zero refund for wheat grain exports.
The wheat flour refund currently stands at five Ecus per tonne.

Talk of a possible cut in the flour refund came amid signs that flour millers, anxious to cover remaining business for the current season, were bidding for licences at five Ecus. There was no immediate confirmation of this.
"I think it is possible that the Commission will cut the refund for flour to zero very soon," a European grain industry source said.

The EU on Monday scrapped a zero refund for soft wheat and durum exports available through a daily bidding channel and replaced it with a nil value entry. The entry implies no prefixation and no monthly increments.
Traders in France said exporters were also rumoured to have bid for these licences despite the greater risk involved, but again there was no confirmation.
